findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the re-identify warning say the trust list must name the (old environment, old key) pair, matching `verify_opcert_record`'s pair check.
evidence: Approach: 'when the verifying environment sets `verify.trusted_opcert_keys`, the (environment, key) pair must be listed or the verdict is `untrusted`'
Warning bullet: 'an environment with `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` trusts them only while its list names the old key'
findings.finding: The proposed re-identify warning wording says an environment with a trust list 'trusts them only while its list names the old key'. The plan's own Approach says the verifier requires the (environment, key) PAIR to be listed. After re-identification, old certificates name the OLD environment, so the trust list must name the (old environment, old key) pair. Listing the old key alone would not be enough. The new message could therefore mislead operators again, just in a different way.
scenarios: An operator re-identifies, then adds only the old key under the new environment name in `verify.trusted_opcert_keys`. Old attestations still come back `untrusted` because the old environment name is not paired with that key.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the bullet to: 'an environment with `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` trusts them only while its list names the old environment paired with the old key'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Rewrite both absence-grep ACs to use `git grep -n -i -E` with `|` alternation, and confirm they print the 4 stale sites before the fix.
evidence: AC: `git grep -n -i 'pinned key\|own or pinned\|unless that key is pinned' -- src` prints nothing.
AC: `git grep -n -i 'out-of-band-pinned\|pinned-key' -- src` prints nothing.
The Context sweep already uses `git grep -n -i -E 'a|b'`, so the ACs are inconsistent with it.
findings.finding: The acceptance-criterion grep commands rely on `\|` alternation inside git grep's default basic regex (BRE). That is a GNU extension: on a platform whose regex library does not support it, the pattern matches the literal text `pinned key|own or pinned|...`. It then prints nothing, so the AC passes vacuously even if the stale wording remains.
scenarios: An executor on macOS or BSD regex runs the AC before the fix, sees empty output, and treats a vacuous pass as proof.
findings.suggested_fix: `git grep -n -i -E 'pinned key|own or pinned|unless that key is pinned|out-of-band-pinned|pinned-key' -- src` prints nothing (and, run before the fix, prints the 4 known sites).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reword the attest/opcert.py:6 opening sentence so it is true of this module: rebar's store verifier (`_opcert_verify.verify_opcert_record`) checks validity on the embedded key plus an optional `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` list, while this module's `verify_opcert` primitive still checks against a keyring the caller supplies, with key validity windows.
evidence: Plan: "`attest/opcert.py:6`: verified by validity of the embedded key, optionally against the verifier's own trust list."

src/rebar/attest/opcert.py:178-193: `def verify_opcert(envelope, ticket_id, material_fingerprint, merged_log_commit, keyring: list[dict], *, kind, principal, storage_anchor_commit, ...)` — 'against ``keyring`` (records of ``{public_key, added_at_log_position, revoked_at_log_position}``)'

src/rebar/attest/opcert.py:12-16: 'Out-of-band keys ... ADR 0125 moves trust to each verifying environment's ``verify.trusted_opcert_keys`` list; :func:`verify_opcert` remains the library primitive for callers that keep keyed eras.'
src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py:171-183: the embedded-key/trust-list model belongs to `verify_opcert_record`, a different module.
findings.finding: The planned rewrite of the attest/opcert.py module docstring's opening sentence ('verified by validity of the embedded key, optionally against the verifier's own trust list') describes the store verifier in `_opcert_verify.verify_opcert_record`, not this module. This module's own public primitive, `verify_opcert`, still checks the envelope against a `keyring` list that the caller passes in, with per-key validity windows (`added_at_log_position`/`revoked_at_log_position`) evaluated at the storage anchor. It never reads the embedded key or `verify.trusted_opcert_keys`. The new sentence would remove one contradiction (with lines 12-15) and add another: it would contradict line 15 ('verify_opcert remains the library primitive for callers that keep keyed eras') and the docstring of `verify_opcert` itself.
scenarios: A developer reads the opcert.py module docstring, assumes `verify_opcert` needs no keyring and checks the embedded key, then calls it wrong or relies on it to enforce `verify.trusted_opcert_keys`.
A later stale-prose sweep finds the opening sentence contradicting the `verify_opcert` docstring and line 15, and the same kind of finding comes back.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the opening clause with something like: '…and rebar's verifier (`rebar._opcert_verify.verify_opcert_record`) accepts it on the public key embedded in its signature, optionally restricted by the verifying environment's `verify.trusted_opcert_keys` list (ADR 0125); this module's :func:`verify_opcert` primitive instead checks against a caller-supplied keyring with key validity windows.'
